sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current official documentation as retrieved 2026-10-12; unpinned
sources.locator: Sections 1, 2.2–2.3, 4 and 11: WAL same-host/single-writer boundary, sidecars, synchronous behavior, WAL-reset bug and affected/fixed versions
sources.observed_operation: Opened primary documentation and read the concurrency/durability passages and WAL-reset bug advisory.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL requires same-host access, has one writer, and treats the WAL as database state. NORMAL can lose committed transactions after power failure. The rare WAL-reset race requires multiple connections with concurrent writes/checkpoints; affected versions through 3.51.2, fixed in 3.51.3+ with named backports.
sources.applicability: Supports local-only WAL and power-loss cautions; adds conditional build/version and test gate if WAL is chosen.
sources.limits: Does not select this application’s storage engine or test its build/filesystem.

sources.title: SQLite PRAGMA synchronous
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current official documentation as retrieved 2026-10-12; unpinned
sources.locator: synchronous matrix and FULL/NORMAL descriptions, approximately lines 824–844
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official PRAGMA reference and located the synchronous matrix.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: FULL in WAL is documented as ACID; NORMAL in WAL remains consistent but may roll back a transaction after power loss. Filesystem and hardware remain relevant to durability.
sources.applicability: Checks the draft’s SQLite power-loss qualification.
sources.limits: Documentation does not qualify a target laptop’s VFS or storage hardware.

sources.title: How To Corrupt An SQLite Database File
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current official documentation as retrieved 2026-10-12; unpinned
sources.locator: Hot journal/WAL pairing and filesystem locking sections
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official caution page and read its WAL-copy and network filesystem conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: After interrupted writes, journal/WAL files must accompany the database; network filesystem locking defects can corrupt concurrent access.
sources.applicability: Checks the draft’s recommendation against syncing a live embedded database as separate files.
sources.limits: Does not establish an atomic protocol between the database and a separate photo store.

sources.title: SQLite Session Extension
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current official documentation as retrieved 2026-10-12; unpinned
sources.locator: Introduction, limitations and conflicts; compatible starting data/schema, primary-key requirements and conflict callbacks
sources.observed_operation: Opened primary docs and read the extension limitations and apply behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Changesets apply to compatible table schemas/starting data; captured tables need declared primary keys; conflicts are handled through app-selected omit/abort/replace behavior. The extension is disabled by default in a build unless enabled.
sources.applicability: Checks the draft’s characterization of Session as a row-delta helper rather than a domain merge policy.
sources.limits: Does not provide this app’s event history or conflict semantics.

sources.title: Apache CouchDB 3.5 conflict model
sources.released_version_or_commit: CouchDB 3.5 stable documentation; page not minor-version pinned
sources.locator: Sections 2.3.1–2.3.4: unidirectional push/pull, retained revision leaves, deterministic winner and conflict retrieval
sources.observed_operation: Opened the primary documentation and inspected the replication and conflict passages.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Independent replicated revisions coexist; a default read chooses one deterministic winner, while conflict-aware retrieval exposes other leaves.
sources.applicability: Checks the CouchDB alternative and need for application conflict review.
sources.limits: Does not evaluate a desktop deployment or guarantee a domain-appropriate winner.

sources.title: CouchDB issue #6126: attachments after delete and recreate
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue opened 2026-09-23 against CouchDB 3.5.2; closed with linked fix
sources.locator: Issue description and reproducer steps, especially delete/recreate same document ID and attachment name with different bytes while the intermediate deletion is not replicated
sources.observed_operation: Opened the upstream issue and read the version, condition and reproducer; did not run it.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The issue reports stale attachment replication in the specified delete/recreate and skipped-intermediate-delete scenario, for transient and certain interrupted continuous replication.
sources.applicability: Supports a narrow attachment regression case and checking content by digest.
sources.limits: A specific reported scenario/version, not evidence of general CouchDB failure; no independent reproduction.

sources.title: Automerge merge rules
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current unversioned official documentation as retrieved 2026-10-12
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the documented map conflict rules.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For concurrent map operations, a set to a key deleted by the other operation remains as the set value; two concurrent sets expose one arbitrary but convergent default.
sources.applicability: Checks the need for application-owned logical tombstones and human conflict presentation.
